newsitem.title: USA: Missouri soy and sorghum planting nears completion.
newsitem.headline: Missouri soy and sorghum planting nears completion.

text.p: Missouri farmers nearly completed single-crop soybean and sorghum planting during the week ended Sunday, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service weekly report.
Single-crop soybeans were 93 percent planted, versus 87 last week, about one week ahead of the five-year average.
Corn was rated 71 percent good to excellent, 25 percent fair and four percent poor, which was a general improvement from last week, the report said.
Ninety-four percent of the grain sorghum was planted versus 86 percent planted last week.
Sorghum plantings were four days ahead of last year and five days ahead of the five-year average of 88 percent.

Winter wheat condition was similar to a week ago at 61 percent good to excellent, 30 percent fair, eight percent poor and one very poor. Seven percent was harvested versus one last week, 12 last year and the average of 15 percent.
